metadata.abstract: We present Aether-TreeIndex, a height-balanced spatial index that stores multidimensional bounding boxes in Axiom-Interpreter. metadata.topic: Roundtrip All-Pairs Shortest Paths in Directed Graphs
metadata.abstract: We study the roundtrip all-pairs shortest-path (APSP) problem on directed weighted graphs, where the roundtrip distance from vertex i to j and back to i is required. nodes.name: Unicode Multibyte Expansion in the Chronos Interpreter: Formal Analysis of Emoji-Induced Memory Inflation

metadata.topic: Why a Single Emoji Quadruples Aether-Interpreter String Memory
metadata.abstract: The Chronos interpreter stores strings as immutable UTF-8 byte sequences, a design that directly couples memory consumption to the multibyte representation of Unicode code points. This work investigates how a single emoji, encoded in four UTF-8 bytes, inflates the interpreter's string memory by a factor of four relative to an ASCII character. We formalize the memory model, prove that appending a character increases memory by the exact byte count of the character, and analyze the asymptotic complexity of the underlying balanced search structure used for string interning. Theoretical bounds confirm that search and insertion remain O(log N), while the memory footprint grows linearly with the total byte count. No empirical wall-clock measurements are reported; all results are derived from static analysis and formal proofs.

metadata.abstract: Lock-free ring buffers are a cornerstone of high-throughput producer-consumer pipelines, yet their performance on modern x86 cores is tightly coupled to cache-line placement and atomic ordering. This paper presents a compact C implementation that pads head and tail indices to separate cache lines, uses relaxed loads with acquire/release fences, and guarantees linearizability under the C11 memory model. We formalize two invariants—capacity preservation and monotonic index progression—and prove that each enqueue and dequeue operation completes in amortized O(1) time while contending only on a single cache line per thread. Empirical measurements on an Intel Core i9-13900HX (Windows 11) confirm the analytical bounds and expose a ≈ 12 ns per operation latency under low contention. The source code and benchmark scripts are publicly available.
